segments.source: Counter Culture says Apollo is a year-round blend made from certified organic washed Ethiopian coffees. The goal is to display Ethiopian citrus and floral character as harvests change, rather than to keep identical lots forever. Calling it an Ethiopian blend does not identify one permanent farm or variety. The current page contains historical harvest periods; match the roast date on your bag to the live record before repeating a particular component split.

For purchase comparison, use the roaster's current category and the tester's attributed sensory experience separately.

segments.source: Counter Culture's general brew advice suggests one gram of coffee to seventeen grams of water for many brewing devices. For a 20 g filter dose that implies 340 g water. It is a practical starting ratio, not a sensory measurement and not an espresso ratio. The roaster also offers cold-brew and other method guidance. Adjust grind and water one variable at a time according to your brewer and the current bag.

segments.source: For espresso, follow the basket and machine's dose guidance, weigh the beverage and dial in independently. A washed medium-roast Ethiopian blend may demand a different grinder setting from the darker coffee you used yesterday; do not blame the coffee merely because the old recipe fails. If espresso is your main daily drink and fruit is only a curiosity, start with 12 oz rather than buying bulk.

segments.source: Counter Culture advises reading the 'Roasted On' date and keeping whole beans sealed away from air, heat and moisture. Because Apollo's component lots rotate, date also helps identify which roaster record corresponds to your bag. An old grocery bag with the same front label may be a worse test of the intended profile than a fresh direct bag.

segments.source: The 12 oz bag supports a small trial. segments.source: Intelligentsia recommends 18 g coffee yielding 45 g espresso, a 1:2.5 ratio. It suggests a fine grind and an even bed in the portafilter. Keep dose fixed first and adjust grind or yield one variable at a time, recording what changed.
